from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Perspective Problem: Maya and the Drone", 
            [
                "Maya and her drone see the world differently.", 
                "The drone is tilted, viewing targets from its perspective.", 
                "We need a translator between these two viewpoints."
            ]
        )
        
        # Grid center for consistent placement
        grid_center = np.array([3.0, -0.3, 0])
        
        # Colors
        MAYA_COLOR = "#87CEEB"
        DRONE_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        VECTOR_COLOR = "#FF0000"
        TEXT_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(MAYA_COLOR)
        
        maya_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": MAYA_COLOR, "stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": MAYA_COLOR}
        )
        self.place_in_area(maya_grid, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        maya_label = Text("Maya's View", font_size=24, color=TEXT_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(maya_label, 'A2', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        maya_dot = Dot(point=grid_center, color=MAYA_COLOR)
        maya_dot_label = Text("Maya", font_size=16, color=MAYA_COLOR).next_to(maya_dot, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            Create(maya_grid),
            Write(maya_label),
            FadeIn(maya_dot),
            Write(maya_dot_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(DRONE_COLOR)
        
        drone_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": DRONE_COLOR, "stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": DRONE_COLOR}
        ).rotate(PI/4).move_to(grid_center)
        
        drone_label = Text("Drone's View", font_size=24, color=TEXT_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(drone_label, 'A5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            Create(drone_grid),
            Write(drone_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(VECTOR_COLOR)
        
        # The vector is 1 unit along the drone's forward axis (rotated 45 degrees)
        # Vector in standard basis: [cos(45), sin(45)]
        target_vec = Arrow(
            start=grid_center,
            end=grid_center + np.array([np.cos(PI/4), np.sin(PI/4), 0]),
            buff=0,
            color=VECTOR_COLOR,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        # Display Coordinates
        # Use Text instead of MathTex to avoid FileNotFoundError when LaTeX is not installed
        drone_coords = Text("Drone: [1, 0]", color=DRONE_COLOR, font_size=24)
        maya_coords = Text("Maya: [0.7, 0.7]", color=MAYA_COLOR, font_size=24)
        
        self.place_at_grid(drone_coords, 'F2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(maya_coords, 'F5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(target_vec),
            Write(drone_coords),
            Write(maya_coords)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define Colors
        COLOR_BLUE = "#87CEEB"
        COLOR_GOLD = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_WHITE = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_GREY = "#666666"

        # Initialize layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite Check: What is a Basis?",
            [
                'A basis provides building blocks for any point.',
                'Usually, we use the standard blue grid.',
                'But any set of independent vectors works.'
            ]
        )

        # Common coordinate plane for right-side visual area
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GREY, "stroke_opacity": 0.3}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "B2", "E5")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_BLUE))
        
        i_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(1, 0), buff=0, color=COLOR_BLUE)
        j_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(0, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_BLUE)
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency error
        i_label = Text("î", color=COLOR_BLUE, font_size=20).next_to(i_vec, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        j_label = Text("ĵ", color=COLOR_BLUE, font_size=20).next_to(j_vec, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(i_vec), 
            GrowArrow(j_vec), 
            Write(i_label), 
            Write(j_label),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_GREY),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_GOLD)
        )
        
        # Basis vectors: b1 = (2, 1), b2 = (-1, 1)
        b1_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(2, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_GOLD)
        b2_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(-1, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_GOLD)
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text
        b1_label = Text("b₁", color=COLOR_GOLD, font_size=20).next_to(b1_vec.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        b2_label = Text("b₂", color=COLOR_GOLD, font_size=20).next_to(b2_vec.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(b1_vec), 
            GrowArrow(b2_vec), 
            Write(b1_label), 
            Write(b2_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_GREY),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_WHITE)
        )
        
        # Point P at (1, 2)
        p_pos = plane.c2p(1, 2)
        p_dot = Dot(p_pos, color=COLOR_WHITE)
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text
        p_label = Text("P", color=COLOR_WHITE, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC).next_to(p_dot, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(p_dot), Write(p_label))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Highlight standard basis sum: P = 1*i + 2*j
        i_comp = Line(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(1,0), color=COLOR_BLUE, stroke_width=6)
        j_comp = Line(plane.c2p(1,0), plane.c2p(1,2), color=COLOR_BLUE, stroke_width=6)
        
        self.play(Create(i_comp))
        self.play(Create(j_comp))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(i_comp), FadeOut(j_comp))
        
        # Highlight gold basis sum: P = 1*b1 + 1*b2
        b1_comp = Line(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(2,1), color=COLOR_GOLD, stroke_width=6)
        b2_comp = Line(plane.c2p(2,1), plane.c2p(1,2), color=COLOR_GOLD, stroke_width=6)
        
        self.play(Create(b1_comp))
        self.play(Create(b2_comp))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial layout setup
        lines = [
            'This vector remains fixed in physical space.',
            'Its coordinates change depending on the chosen grid.',
            'The vector stays; only the ruler moves.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Core Concept: One Vector, Two Names", lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_VECTOR = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_STD_GRID = "#87CEEB"
        COLOR_SLANTED_GRID = "#FFD700"

        # Center of the animation area
        center_pos = self.grid["C3"] + (self.grid["D4"] - self.grid["C3"]) / 2

        # 1. Create Standard Plane
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": COLOR_STD_GRID, "stroke_opacity": 0.5}
        ).move_to(center_pos)

        # 2. Create the Vector (Target: 1 unit right, 1 unit up)
        vector = Arrow(
            start=plane.coords_to_point(0, 0),
            end=plane.coords_to_point(1, 1),
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_VECTOR,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        label = Text("v", color=COLOR_VECTOR).next_to(vector.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation Sequence
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(GrowArrow(vector), Write(label))
        self.wait(1)

        # Create slanted transformation (Basis change)
        # Vector remains visually fixed, plane transforms
        slanted_plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": COLOR_SLANTED_GRID, "stroke_opacity": 0.6}
        ).move_to(center_pos).apply_matrix([[1, 0.5], [0.3, 1]])

        self.play(
            Transform(plane, slanted_plane),
            label.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.2),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Set background
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        
        # Setup Title
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Setup Lecture Content (Left Side)
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.lecture.scale(0.85).to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define animation grid for the right side (used for placing visual elements)
        self.grid_map = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        # The right side occupies roughly x = 1 to 6
        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid_map[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        if grid_pos in self.grid_map:
            mobject.move_to(self.grid_map[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        # 1. Layout Initialization
        lecture_content = [
            "- Understanding Change of Basis",
            "- Linear Transformation Properties",
            "- Defining Custom Basis Vectors",
            "- Mapping to the New System",
            "- Visualizing the Transformation"
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Change of Basis: Vector Spaces", lecture_content)

        # 2. Visualization Setup (Coordinate Plane on the right)
        # Center the plane around the middle of our grid map (roughly C4/D4)
        visual_center = self.grid_map["C4"] + DOWN * 0.2
        
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"stroke_width": 2},
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        ).move_to(visual_center)

        # Standard basis vectors
        basis_i = Vector([1, 0], color=BLUE).shift(visual_center)
        basis_j = Vector([0, 1], color=RED).shift(visual_center)
        
        # Labels for standard basis - Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency
        label_i = Text("i", slant=ITALIC, color=BLUE, font_size=20).next_to(basis_i, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        label_j = Text("j", slant=ITALIC, color=RED, font_size=20).next_to(basis_j, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        # 3. Animation Sequence
        self.play(Write(self.title))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Animate lecture points
        for line in self.lecture:
            self.play(FadeIn(line, shift=RIGHT * 0.2), run_time=0.6)
        
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Show the grid and standard basis
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(basis_i), 
            GrowArrow(basis_j),
            Write(label_i),
            Write(label_j)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Define new basis vectors (Alternative Basis)
        # b1 = [1, 0.5], b2 = [-0.5, 1]
        new_basis_i = Vector([1, 0.5], color=YELLOW).shift(visual_center)
        new_basis_j = Vector([-0.5, 1], color=GOLD).shift(visual_center)
        
        new_label = Text("Transformation Applied", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(new_label, "F4")

        # Perform the change of basis animation
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(basis_i, new_basis_i),
            ReplacementTransform(basis_j, new_basis_j),
            FadeOut(label_i),
            FadeOut(label_j),
            plane.animate.apply_matrix([[1, -0.5], [0.5, 1]]),
            Write(new_label),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Colors
        SKY_BLUE = "#87CEEB"
        GOLD = "#FFD700"
        RED = "#FF0000"
        
        lecture_lines = [
            'Matrix multiplication physically warps the entire grid.',
            'The standard grid morphs into the new basis.',
            'Watch how the coordinate lines bend and stretch.',
            'The vector arrow stays still while the grid shifts.',
            'Coordinates change inversely to keep the vector fixed.'
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("The Visual Transformation: Warping the Grid", lecture_lines)
        
        # Transformation matrix: Shear M = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
        matrix = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
        
        # Animation Area Center
        anim_center = (self.grid["A1"] + self.grid["F6"]) / 2
        
        # 1. Initialize Grid
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": SKY_BLUE, "stroke_width": 2, "stroke_opacity": 0.5},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": WHITE, "stroke_width": 2}
        ).scale(0.7).move_to(anim_center)
        
        # 2. Initialize Vector (Fixed in screen space)
        target_vec_pos = plane.c2p(1, 1)
        vector = Arrow(plane.get_origin(), target_vec_pos, buff=0, color=RED, stroke_width=5)
        
        # 3. Initialize Labels
        # CHANGED: Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "Practical Application: Why Bother?"
        lines = [
            'Some problems are simpler in a custom basis.',
            "An eagle's flight is easy along its path.",
            'Aligning the basis simplifies complex diagonal motion.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        VEC_COLOR = YELLOW
        EAGLE_COLOR = WHITE
        AXIS_COLOR = GREY_B

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line 1: Highlighted
        self.lecture[0].set_color(VEC_COLOR)

        # Coordinate Plane
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5,
            axis_config={"color": AXIS_COLOR, "include_tip": True},
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3}
        )
        
        # Velocity parameters (2, 1.5) -> magnitude 2.5, angle ~36.87 degrees
        vx, vy = 2.0, 1.5
        mag = np.sqrt(vx**2 + vy**2)
        angle = np.arctan2(vy, vx)
        
        origin_pt = plane.c2p(0, 0, 0)
        end_pt = plane.c2p(vx, vy, 0)
        
        # Velocity Vector
        velocity_vec = Arrow(origin_pt, end_pt, buff=0, color=VEC_COLOR, stroke_width=4)
        
        # Eagle Icon (Triangle)
        eagle_icon = Triangle(color=EAGLE_COLOR, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.12).move_to(end_pt).rotate(angle)
        eagle_text = Text("Eagle", font_size=18, color=EAGLE_COLOR).next_to(eagle_icon, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        # Standard basis labels (Replacing MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency)
        coord_label = Text(
            "v = [2.0, 1.5]", 
            font_size=32, color=VEC_COLOR
        )
        self.place_at_grid(coord_label, "B5")
        
        # Group the world to rotate together
        world = VGroup(plane, velocity_vec, eagle_icon, eagle_text)
        self.place_in_area(world, "A2", "F6")
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(world),
            Write(coord_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition highlights
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(VEC_COLOR)
        
        # Rotate world by negative the eagle's angle to align x-axis with flight path
        rotation_angle = -angle
        
        self.play(
            Rotate(world, angle=rotation_angle, about_point=plane.c2p(0,0,0)),
            # Counter-rotate text to keep it readable
            Rotate(eagle_text, angle=-rotation_angle, about_point=eagle_text.get_center()),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition highlights
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(VEC_COLOR)
        
        # New basis coordinates (Replacing MathTex with Text)
        new_coord_label = Text(
            "v' = [2.5, 0]", 
            font_size=32, color=VEC_COLOR
        )
        new_coord_label.move_to(coord_label.get_center())
        
        # Simple highlight of the aligned axis
        path_highlight = Line(
            plane.c2p(0,0,0), 
            plane.c2p(2.5, 0, 0), 
            color=VEC_COLOR, 
            stroke_width=6, 
            stroke_opacity=0.5
        )
        # Add highlight to world so it stays in the rotated frame
        world.add(path_highlight)

        self.play(
            Transform(coord_label, new_coord_label),
            FadeIn(path_highlight),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Summary & The 'Golden Rule' Formula", 
            [
                'Use P to move from new to standard.', 
                'The inverse, P-inverse, takes us back again.', 
                'This formula links every perspective together.', 
                'Coordinates are relative, but the vector is absolute.', 
                'Choose the basis that makes your math easy.'
            ]
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        # Use Text instead of MathTex to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        formula_std = Text(
            "[x]Std = P [x]New",
            color="#00FF00",
            font_size=32
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula_std, "A1", "B6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula_std))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF8C00"))
        
        # Use Text instead of MathTex to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        formula_new = Text(
            "[x]New = P^-1 [x]Std",
            color="#FF8C00",
            font_size=32
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula_new, "C1", "D6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula_new))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Flowchart Boxes
        drone_box = VGroup(
            RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.6, width=2.2, color=WHITE),

        )
        maya_box = VGroup(
            RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.6, width=2.2, color=WHITE),
            Text("Maya's View", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        )
        
        self.place_at_grid(drone_box, "E2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(maya_box, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Arrow Drone -> Maya (P)
        arrow_top = Arrow(
            start=drone_box.get_right(), 
            end=maya_box.get_left(), 
            buff=0.1,

        )

        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: Change of Basis: Viewing the World through Different Lenses

sections.title: The Perspective Problem: Maya and the Drone
sections.content: Introduce the motivation for change of basis. Different observers see the same vector from different perspectives. We need a 'translator' between these perspectives.
sections.example: Maya (Character) is standing at (0,0) on a standard grid. Her Drone (Device) is tilted 45 degrees. When the Drone sees a target 1 unit 'forward' in its own view, Maya sees it at a diagonal. We need to describe the target's location in both 'Maya-language' and 'Drone-language'.

sections.title: Prerequisite Check: What is a Basis?
sections.content: Briefly review that a basis is a set of 'building block' vectors (v1, v2) that can reach any point via linear combinations. Emphasize the 'Standard Basis' (i, j).
sections.example: Visual: Show the standard grid (i, j) in blue. Then overlay a slanted, stretched grid (b1, b2) in gold. Explain that any point P can be written as 'x units of i + y units of j' OR 'a units of b1 + b units of b2'.

sections.title: The Core Concept: One Vector, Two Names
sections.content: Define the notation [x]_B. A vector 'x' is an physical arrow in space; its 'coordinates' are just the coefficients relative to a specific basis B.
sections.example: Animation: A single red arrow exists in space. When the blue grid (Basis B1) is active, its coordinates are (3, 2). When the blue grid fades and the gold grid (Basis B2) appears, the same arrow now has coordinates (1, 1). The arrow didn't move; the ruler did.

sections.title: The Change of Basis Matrix (The Translator)
sections.content: Introduce the Transition Matrix P. Explain that P is composed of the vectors of the 'New' basis expressed in the 'Old' basis coordinates.
sections.example: If the Drone's 'Forward' vector is (0.7, 0.7) in Maya's coordinates and its 'Side' vector is (-0.7, 0.7), these become the columns of Matrix P. Multiplying the Drone's coordinates by P 'translates' them back to Maya's world.

sections.title: The Visual Transformation: Warping the Grid
sections.content: Use animation to show how the matrix multiplication physically maps one coordinate system onto another. This reinforces the 'Linear Map' intuition.
sections.example: Show the Standard Grid morphing/shearing into the new Basis Grid. As the grid lines bend, show how the coordinate numbers of our target point change inversely to keep the vector arrow pointing at the same spot in physical space.

sections.title: Practical Application: Why Bother?
sections.content: Explain that some problems (like stretching or rotating objects) are 'ugly' in the standard basis but 'beautifully simple' in a basis aligned with the object.
sections.example: An Eagle (Animal) flying diagonally. In the standard North-East basis, its velocity has complex components. But if we change the basis to be 'Along the Eagle's Path' and 'Perpendicular to it', the velocity is simply (Speed, 0). Change of basis simplifies the math.

sections.title: Summary & The 'Golden Rule' Formula
sections.content: Summarize the relationship: [x]_Standard = P * [x]_New. Emphasize that to go the other way, we use the Inverse Matrix (P^-1).
sections.example: Closing Graphic: A flowchart showing: [Drone View] --(Multiply by P)--> [Maya's View] and [Maya's View] --(Multiply by P inverse)--> [Drone View].
